ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the regular pentagon ABCDE is inscribed in $\odot O$. Connecting AC, what is the degree measure of $\angle ACD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect OA, OE, OD, \\
since a regular pentagon ABCDE is inscribed in the circle $O$, \\
therefore, $\angle AOE = \angle DOE = \frac{360^\circ}{5} = 72^\circ$, \\
hence, $\angle ACD = \frac{1}{2} \angle AOD = \boxed{72^\circ}$.

From the text, use that ABCDE is a regular pentagon inscribed in circle O. Since five equal sides cut the circle into five equal arcs, each minor arc/central angle is 360°/5 = 72°. method.method_draft: Read the figure as a regular pentagon with diagonal AC drawn from A to C, splitting the interior angle at C into ∠BCA and ∠ACD. From the text, use regularity of ABCDE. The interior angle of a regular pentagon is (5−2)·180°/5 = 108°, so ∠BCD = 108°. In triangle ABC, sides AB and BC are equal because they are sides of the regular pentagon, so triangle ABC is isosceles. Its angle at B is the pentagon interior angle ∠ABC = 108°, hence each base angle is (180°−108°)/2 = 36°, so ∠BCA = 36°. Therefore ∠ACD = ∠BCD − ∠BCA = 108° − 36° = 72°.
